business_problem: SAS needed to modernize a fragmented security estate that lacked behavioral detection, 24-hour monitoring, centralized governance, and scalable response processes, making it harder for the airline to protect digital operations as cloud adoption and cyber threats increased.
solution_summary: SAS and TCS expanded an existing IT relationship into an intelligence-driven cybersecurity operating model. TCS migrated SAS's SIEM and EDR tooling into a unified security platform, added 24-hour monitoring, and connected multiple threat intelligence platforms so indicators of compromise could be enriched automatically. On top of that foundation, the teams built anomaly-based detection playbooks, automated investigation workflows to reduce MTTD and MTTR, and integrated high-severity alerting with internal communications and email channels for faster escalation. Supporting controls such as an Attack Surface Management platform, centralized vulnerability dashboards, threat hunting on SIEM and EDR telemetry, and a client-based cloud proxy platform gave SAS broader visibility across infrastructure, network, and application risk. The result was a security operations capability that uses AI-driven detection and workflow automation as a core operating layer rather than an isolated pilot.

data_flow: Endpoint, infrastructure, network, and application telemetry is collected through EDR and SIEM, enriched automatically with threat intelligence, and processed by anomaly-based detection playbooks and automated investigation workflows. High-severity alerts are pushed into internal communications and email channels, while dashboards, attack-surface monitoring, and threat hunting use the same telemetry to guide remediation and compliance oversight.
business_outcome: SAS gained a more resilient, always-on security operating model with better visibility, faster detection and response, improved compliance reporting, and stronger control over cyber risk as it continues its digital-first airline transformation.
